metadata.title: KORUM · Where good ideas add up and get done
metadata.description: Ideas box, all-or-nothing campaigns and QR ticketing for schools, clubs and cultural organisations. If the goal is not reached, 100% is refunded.

common.footerNote: KORUM is a technology platform. Payments and refunds are handled by PAYCOMET.

home.eyebrow: For schools, clubs and cultural organisations
home.title: Where your school or club’s good ideas add up and come true.
home.subtitle: The independent platform for your community to propose, decide and fund improvements: all-or-nothing campaigns with automatic refunds if the goal is not reached, digital ticketing with QR codes, and complete freedom to choose your supplier. No sign-up fee and no handling cash.
home.ctaSignup: 🏫 Register my school, parents’ association or club for free
home.badgeRefund: If the goal is not reached, 100% is refunded
home.badgeProvider: The organisation freely chooses its supplier
home.badgePayments: Payments and refunds handled by PAYCOMET

finder.title: Find your school or club
finder.intro: If your community is already on KORUM, open its page to see its initiatives.

items.title: Propose and gather signatures
items.text: Any family proposes an improvement and the community backs it with a signature.

items.title: Double signature by the organisation
items.text: Two people from the organisation approve it, and you freely choose your supplier.

items.title: Families contribute in 10 seconds
items.text: Families pay with Bizum or card. It is all or nothing: if the goal is not reached, 100% is refunded.

items.title: Enjoy the Before and After
items.text: Once the goal is reached, the improvement is paid for and the whole community sees the result.

calculator.title: How much needs to be raised?
calculator.intro: Work out your project’s goal with the same rules the platform uses. With an average contribution of €15 to €25 and a few neighbourhood businesses, goals are usually within reach.

cards.title: Organisations
bullets: No cash and no spreadsheets
Joint double signature by two people
Direct payment to the organisation or its supplier
Model 182 ready in one click if the organisation falls under Law 49/2002
Entry-check mode with QR codes and yearly medals

cards.title: Families
bullets: Contribute in 10 seconds, no sign-up
Automatic 100% refund if the goal is not reached
Class or team challenges, always positive
QR tickets on your phone

cards.title: Local businesses
bullets: Visibility among neighbourhood families
Gold, Silver or Bronze category
100% of the sponsorship reaches the initiative
Sponsorship receipt and invoice for the fee, straight away

money.title: How money is handled
money.text: Payments are processed by PAYCOMET, a payment institution authorised by the Bank of Spain. KORUM is the technology: it never holds your money. If an initiative does not reach its goal, 100% is refunded to each person.
money.link: Read more about security and transparency

final.title: Start today, free to register
final.text: Register your organisation in three steps and start collecting your community’s ideas.

error.title: Something didn't go as expected
error.description: We couldn't load this page. Please try again in a few seconds.

notFound.title: We can't find this page
notFound.description: The link may be mistyped or the page may no longer exist.

audit.ipBurst: ⚠️ Many signatures from the same network in under 10 minutes.
audit.secondAccount: 2nd family account on the same device (parent, verified).
audit.tooManyAccounts: ⚠️ Account number {n} signing from the same device (maximum 2 per family).

export.title: Your data at KORUM
export.intro: A copy of the personal data KORUM holds about you (GDPR, articles 15 and 20). The accompanying JSON file contains the same data in a format you can take to another service.

sections.ideaProposals: Idea proposals and chat with the school

common.tagline: Where good ideas add up and get done.
common.buttonFallback: If the button does not work, copy this link into your browser:
common.footerTransactional: You are receiving this because you made a transaction with {organization} through KORUM. This is a service message, not marketing.
common.footerAccount: You are receiving this because an action was requested on your KORUM account. This is a service message, not marketing.
common.footerPlatform: KORUM is a technology platform and does not hold funds. Payments and refunds are handled by PAYCOMET.
common.footerOrganization: You are receiving this because you manage {organization} on KORUM. This is a service message, not marketing.

magicLink.subject: Your link to sign in to KORUM
magicLink.preheader: One click and you are in.
magicLink.title: Sign in to KORUM
magicLink.body: Press the button to sign in. The link expires in {minutes} minutes and works only once.
magicLink.footnote: If this was not you, ignore this email: nobody gets in without pressing the link.

otp.subject: Your KORUM access code
otp.title: Your access code
otp.body: Enter this code to sign in. It expires in {minutes} minutes.
otp.footnote: If you did not ask for it, ignore this message and do not share the code with anyone.

invitation.subject: You're invited to co-sign for {organization} on KORUM
invitation.preheader: Create your password and turn on two-step verification.
invitation.title: {organization} is counting on you
invitation.body: You have been appointed {role} of {organization}. Your signature, together with that of the person who runs the organisation, is needed to approve ideas and release funds: no single person can do it alone.
invitation.bodyPlatform: A KORUM Super-Admin account has been created with this email. Create your password to access the console.
invitation.security: The link expires in {hours} hours and works only once. When you sign in we will ask you to turn on two-step verification with a phone app.
invitation.footnote: Don't recognise this invitation or this organisation? Ignore this email: unless you accept it, you won't have any role and nothing will be activated.

receipt.subject: Receipt for your contribution to “{initiative}”
receipt.preheader: Thanks for chipping in. Here is your receipt.
receipt.title: Thank you for chipping in!
receipt.body: We have received your contribution of {amount} to “{initiative}”, from {organization}.
receipt.guarantee: The money is held by Paycomet until the goal is reached. If the initiative does not succeed, we refund 100% of what you paid to the same payment method.
receipt.fiscalCertificate: If you provided your tax ID, the part donated to the organisation will be included in your donation tax certificate (Spanish Law 49/2002), which you can download in January. The voluntary contribution to KORUM does not count towards the certificate.
receipt.fiscalReceipt: Keep this email: it works as a personalised proof of your contribution.

ticket.bodyEvent: Show the QR code at the door. It is attached to this email as an image, and you can also open it with the button.
ticket.bodyRaffle: Your numbers are in the draw. Keep this email: the attached QR code identifies you if you win.
ticket.footnote: The QR code is personal: do not post it on social media. It can be used only once; if someone else uses it first, your ticket will no longer be valid.

pinRevoked.subject: We have revoked the door PIN for “{initiative}”
pinRevoked.preheader: For security. The door keeps running.
pinRevoked.title: Door PIN revoked
pinRevoked.body: After too many failed attempts, we revoked the door PIN for “{initiative}”. Sessions that were already open keep working, so the door does not stop.

goalReached.subject: “{initiative}” has reached its goal!
goalReached.preheader: Time to celebrate: it is done.
goalReached.title: Goal reached!
goalReached.body: “{initiative}” has reached the {goal} it needed thanks to {count, plural, one {# contribution} other {# contributions}}.
goalReached.next: The next step is settlement: it needs the signatures of two different people from the organisation.

expired.subject: “{initiative}” did not reach its goal
expired.preheader: You can resize it or refund 100%.
expired.title: The campaign ended short of its goal
expired.body: “{initiative}” expired with {raised} of the {goal} needed. No contribution is lost: you can resize the initiative or refund 100% to families.

refund.subject: We have refunded your payment for “{initiative}”
refund.preheader: The amount is on its way back to your payment method.
refund.title: Refund issued
refund.body: We have refunded {amount} to the same payment method you paid with.
refund.timing: Depending on your card issuer or payment app, it can take a few business days to show up.

doubleCheck.subject: Your signature is needed at {organization}
doubleCheck.title: We need your signature
doubleCheck.body: To complete this operation, two signatures from different people of the organisation are needed. Open the link while signed in and enter the 6-digit code. It expires on {expires}.
doubleCheck.footnote: The link works once. If you were not expecting this signature, do not complete it and tell the other signer.

expiring.subject: {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}} left to settle “{initiative}”
expiring.preheader: Paycomet only allows paying out funds for 90 days.
expiring.title: The settlement deadline is running out
expiring.body: Paycomet only allows paying out funds during the 90 days after the first charge. Time left for “{initiative}”: {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}}. If it is not settled in time, it will have to be resolved by hand.

expired.subject: The payout window for “{initiative}” has expired
expired.preheader: Our team will help you sort it out.
expired.title: The payout window has expired
expired.body: The 90 days that Paycomet allows for paying out the funds of “{initiative}” have passed. The KORUM team will review the case and contact you.

renewalNotice.subject: Your Friendly Business badge for {organization} expires on {date}
renewalNotice.preheader: Renew in one click without losing a single day.
renewalNotice.title: Your badge expires soon
renewalNotice.body: Your Friendly Business badge for {organization} ({amount} sponsorship) expires on {date}. We never charge you automatically: if you want to carry on, renew with the button below. Your new year starts when the current one ends, so you do not lose a single day.

welcome.subject: You’re now a Friendly business of {organization}!
welcome.preheader: Your badge is already on their page.
welcome.title: Welcome to the friendly businesses!
welcome.body: {organization} has approved your sponsorship. Your {level} badge now appears on its friendly businesses page and is valid until {date}.
welcome.matching: Your Matching 2x pool is now active: every donation from a family is doubled with it until it runs out.
welcome.documents: The button takes you to your sponsorship receipt and, from there, to the management invoice and the poster for your shop window. Keep this email: the link is personal. If you want to share the poster, share only its page: it doesn’t open your documents.

rejected.subject: {organization} has not accepted your sponsorship
rejected.preheader: We are refunding 100% of what you paid.
rejected.title: Your sponsorship has not been accepted
rejected.body: {organization} has reviewed your sponsorship and has not accepted it. We are refunding 100% of what you paid ({amount}: sponsorship, management and VAT) to the same payment method.
rejected.rectified: We have cancelled the management invoice with a corrective invoice.
rejected.footnote: Paycomet processes the refund and it may take a few days to appear on your payment method. We’ll let you know when it goes through.

renewalLink.subject: Your Friendly Business badge for {organization} has expired
renewalLink.preheader: You can still renew with this link.
renewalLink.title: Shall we carry on for another year?
renewalLink.body: Your Friendly Business badge for {organization} ({amount} sponsorship) expired on {date}. If you would like to keep supporting its families, you can renew with the button below until {until}. We never charge you automatically.

renewal.footnote: Payment is made on the secure page of PAYCOMET, the authorised payment institution that processes the charge. 100% of your sponsorship goes to the organisation’s campaigns according to its rule; the advertising management fee and its VAT are separate, with their own invoice.

renewed.subject: Renewed: you are still a Friendly Business of {organization}
renewed.title: Thank you for another year!
renewed.body: We have received your renewal. Your {level} Friendly Business badge for {organization} is valid until {date}.
renewed.placed: Your {amount} in full is already adding up in: {list}.
renewed.chained: You had already renewed this year: this second payment renews the following year, until {date}. If it was a mistake, write to us from the support page.

reassigned.subject: Your sponsorship of {organization} keeps adding up
reassigned.preheader: Your contribution has moved to another campaign.
reassigned.title: Your contribution keeps adding up
reassigned.body: Following the rule set by {organization}, your {amount} in full has gone to: {list}.
reassigned.why: This is how sponsorship works: if the campaign you supported does not go ahead or, when it ends, has part of your Matching 2x contribution left over, your money is not lost: it moves to another campaign of the organisation. You still appear as a friendly business.
reassigned.listMore: {list} and {more, plural, one {# more} other {# more}}

creditPool.subject: Your sponsorship of {organization} is waiting for a new campaign
creditPool.preheader: Your contribution is still held by PAYCOMET, with a deadline.
creditPool.title: Your contribution is waiting for a campaign
creditPool.bodyWaiting: Right now {organization} has no campaign to take your {amount} to. It remains held by PAYCOMET until {deadline}: as soon as a campaign opens, it will go there. If it has not been placed by then, it will go to the organisation for its activities this school year.
creditPool.bodyManual: {organization} will choose which campaign to take your {amount} to. It remains held by PAYCOMET until {deadline}; if it has not been placed by then, it will go to the organisation for its activities this school year.
creditPool.visible: In the meantime you still appear as a friendly business.

renewalInvite.subject: {organization} invites you to remain a Friendly business
renewalInvite.preheader: An invitation, with no commitment and no automatic charges.
renewalInvite.title: Shall we carry on for another year?
renewalInvite.body: {organization} would like to invite you to renew your Friendly business badge ({amount} sponsorship), which {verb} on {date}. It is only an invitation: if you would like to continue, you can renew it with the button below until {until}. There are no automatic charges and we will not write to you about this again this year.

toEntityFund.subject: Your contribution goes to {organization} for its activities
toEntityFund.preheader: There was no campaign to take it to in time.
toEntityFund.title: Your contribution keeps adding up
toEntityFund.body: {organization} had no campaign to take your {amount} to before its deadline. That is why it goes to its Activity Fund: the organisation will use it for its activities this school year, with the signature of both of its officers.
toEntityFund.why: This is what the sponsorship terms provide: your contribution is for the organisation and is not returned once the business has been accepted. Your advertising stays the same.

awaitingDecision.subject: A friendly business is waiting for your decision at {organization}
awaitingDecision.preheader: Its money cannot be moved until you decide.
awaitingDecision.title: Your decision on a business is pending
awaitingDecision.body: A business has paid its {amount} sponsorship in a campaign that is no longer raising money. Until you decide whether to accept it, its money cannot be taken to another campaign. If you accept it after {deadline}, it can only go to your Activity Fund; if you do not accept it, we will refund 100%.
awaitingDecision.what: If you accept it before then, it will go to your campaigns according to your rule.

lateReceived.subject: Your payment to {organization} arrived after the campaign had closed
lateReceived.preheader: The organisation will decide; your money is still held by PAYCOMET.
lateReceived.title: Your payment arrived a little late
lateReceived.body: We have received your {amount} sponsorship, but when it arrived the campaign of {organization} was no longer raising money. Your money is still held by PAYCOMET while the organisation decides whether to accept you as a friendly business.
lateReceived.next: If {organization} accepts you, your contribution will go to another of its campaigns or, if there is none in time, to its Activity Fund. If it does not accept you, we will refund 100% of what you paid, including the management fee and its VAT.

certificateReady.subject: Your {year} tax certificate of donation is ready
certificateReady.title: Your tax certificate is ready
certificateReady.body: You can now download the tax certificate for your {year} donations (Law 49/2002) for your income tax return.

model182.subject: Reminder: Modelo 182 (Form 182) for {year}
model182.preheader: It must be filed by 31 January.
model182.title: Time to prepare Modelo 182
model182.body: Modelo 182 (Form 182), with the {year} donations, must be filed by 31 January. You can already download it from the organisation dashboard.

inactivity.subject: Your KORUM account will be deleted on {date} unless you return
inactivity.preheader: Signing in is enough to keep it.
inactivity.title: We have not seen you in a while
inactivity.body: You have not signed in to KORUM for over three years. Unless you sign in before {date}, we will delete your account and personal data.
inactivity.kept: By legal obligation we keep the minimum accounting and tax data of your contributions, unlinked from your account.
inactivity.keep: To keep it, just sign in.

passkeyAdded.subject: A passkey has been added to your account
passkeyAdded.preheader: If it wasn't you, let us know.
passkeyAdded.title: New passkey
passkeyAdded.body: A passkey has just been added to your KORUM account: it can be used to sign in without an email or password. If it was you, there's nothing you need to do.
passkeyAdded.footnote: If it wasn't you, go to My account, remove the passkey and contact support.

charged.subject: Your monthly pledge to {organization} has arrived
charged.title: You’re adding up again this month!
charged.body: We have charged your monthly pledge of {amount} and all of it went to “{initiative}”, run by {organization}.
charged.fiscalCertificate: If you gave your tax ID when you set it up, each donated month will be included in your donation tax certificate (Spanish Law 49/2002), available to download in January. The Piggy Bank handling fee does not count towards the certificate.

skipped.subject: We have not charged your pledge to {organization} this month
skipped.preheader: There was no campaign raising funds.
skipped.title: No charge this month
skipped.body: {organization} has no campaign raising funds right now, so we have not charged the {amount} of your monthly pledge this month.
skipped.next: You don’t need to do anything: next month we will try again with whichever campaign is open.
skipped.last: This was the last month of your pledge, so it has now ended. If you want to continue, you can set up a new one in your Piggy Bank.

failed.subject: We could not charge your monthly pledge to {organization}
failed.title: This month’s charge did not go through
failed.body: We tried to charge your monthly pledge of {amount} for {organization} and it was not possible. You have not been charged anything.
failed.paused: We have paused your pledge so we don’t keep trying with a card that doesn’t work. If you want to continue, you can resume it in your Piggy Bank.
failed.cardGone: The saved card can no longer be used. If you want to keep giving every month, cancel this pledge and set up a new one in your Piggy Bank.

received.subject: We have received your question {code}
received.preheader: We will answer as soon as we can.
received.title: Question received
received.bodyOrganization: We have received your question and passed it to the school, which will answer. Keep this code in case you need to refer to it.
received.bodyPlatform: We have received your question and the KORUM team will answer. Keep this code in case you need to refer to it.
received.rectification: We have also opened your personal data rectification request: we will deal with it within one month at most.

quorumReached.subject: Quorum reached: “{title}” is waiting for your dual sign-off
quorumReached.preheader: An idea in the ideas box now has enough signatures.
quorumReached.title: An idea has reached the quorum!
quorumReached.body: The proposal “{title}” ({alias}) now has the verified signatures your organisation requires.
quorumReached.next: To turn it into an initiative, two signatures are needed: the head’s and the co-signer’s. Go to Approvals and request your signing link.

reply.subject: {organization} has replied to your proposal
reply.preheader: You have a new message about your idea.
reply.title: You have a new message
reply.body: {organization} has replied to your proposal {alias}. For your privacy we do not copy the message here: read it in your account.

rejected.subject: News about your proposal at {organization}
rejected.title: Your proposal has not gone ahead
rejected.body: {organization} has reviewed your proposal {alias} and could not approve it. They explain why in the chat in your account. Thank you for taking part!

approved.subject: Your proposal is now collecting signatures at {organization}
approved.preheader: The organisation has published your idea in the ideas box.
approved.title: Your idea is now in the ideas box!
approved.body: {organization} has reviewed your proposal {alias} and published it so families can support it with their signature. Share it to help it reach the minimum.
approved.edited: The organisation edited the text when publishing it. You can see it in your account and ask them in the chat if something does not look right.

centerReplied.footnote: You are receiving this notice because you suggested an idea in the organisation’s ideas box.

requested.subject: {organization}: a handover of your signing seat has been proposed
requested.preheader: We need your approval before inviting anyone.
requested.title: Your replacement has been proposed
requested.body: The other person who signs for {organization} proposes that someone else takes your seat. Open the dashboard to see who and give your approval with your code, or decline it. If you do nothing, the proposal expires in 7 days and you keep signing.

declined.subject: {organization}: the handover was not approved
declined.title: Handover declined
declined.body: The person whose seat you proposed to hand over at {organization} did not approve it. The same two people keep signing.

completedLeaving.subject: {organization}: you no longer sign for the organisation
completedLeaving.preheader: Your replacement has accepted the position.
completedLeaving.title: Handover complete
completedLeaving.body: Your replacement at {organization} has accepted the position ({role}). From now on you no longer sign for the organisation and your pending signatures are no longer valid. Thank you for your work.

completedStaying.subject: {organization}: there is a new person on the signing team
completedStaying.title: New signer
completedStaying.body: A handover has been completed at {organization}: the new person now holds their seat ({role}). The outgoing person's pending signatures are no longer valid: if anything was half-way, request the signature again.

handover.why: If you do not recognise this change, contact support as soon as possible.

activityFund.how: To receive it in your account, one of the two signers requests the payout in the panel, stating what the money will be used for, and you both sign with your code.

received.subject: {amount} has gone to the Activity Fund of {organization}
received.preheader: Money from a friendly business for your activities.
received.title: New money in your Activity Fund
received.body: {amount} from a friendly business has gone to your Activity Fund: there was no campaign to take it to in time. It is money for the organisation’s activities. Pay it out before {deadline}: after that, PAYCOMET could no longer send it.

reminder.subject: Pay out the Activity Fund of {organization} before {deadline}
reminder.preheader: PAYCOMET’s deadline to send the money is running out.
reminder.title: The deadline to pay out the Fund is running out
reminder.body: Your Activity Fund holds {amount} that has not been paid out. PAYCOMET can only send it to your account until {deadline}.
reminder.footnote: If you have already requested the payout, both signatures still need to be completed.

paid.subject: {amount} from the Activity Fund sent to {organization}
paid.preheader: The payout is on its way to your account.
paid.title: Activity Fund paid out
paid.body: PAYCOMET has sent the {amount} of payout {reference} of the Activity Fund to the organisation’s account.
paid.receipt: In the panel you have its PDF receipt, with the purpose you signed and which businesses the money came from.

executed.subject: Payout done: {amount} from “{initiative}”
executed.preheader: Both signatures are in and the money is on its way.
executed.title: Payout done!
executed.bodyORGANIZATION: PAYCOMET has sent {amount} from the piggy bank of “{initiative}” to the organisation’s account. You can now pay the supplier with their invoice.
executed.bodyPROVIDER: PAYCOMET has sent {amount} from the piggy bank of “{initiative}” directly to the supplier you chose.
executed.next: The last step: upload the Before and After photos and a thank-you message. Once both photos are there, the families who contributed will get a notice to see them.

changed.subject: Payout {reference} for “{initiative}” has changed
changed.preheader: Your previous signature is no longer valid: check the details before signing again.
changed.title: The payout has changed
changed.body: The other signatory has changed the destination, the invoice or the figures of the payout for “{initiative}”. Previous signatures are no longer valid.
changed.check: Check in Payouts where the money goes and the invoice before signing again. If you don’t recognise the change, don’t sign and contact support.

goalReached.subject: We did it! “{initiative}”
goalReached.preheader: {organization} has reached 100% thanks to you and the other families.
goalReached.title: We did it!
goalReached.body: “{initiative}” by {organization} has reached its goal thanks to {count, plural, one {one contribution: yours} other {# contributions, and one of them is yours}}. Thank you!
goalReached.next: The money stays in the initiative’s piggy bank at PAYCOMET until two people from {organization} sign its payout. Once it’s done, we’ll show you the Before and After.

photos.subject: See how it turned out: “{initiative}”
photos.preheader: The Before and After photos are here.
photos.title: See how it turned out
photos.body: {organization} has published the Before and After photos of “{initiative}”, the initiative you contributed to.
photos.thanks: Thank you for helping make it happen.

decided.refundPreheader: A signatory has decided to refund what was raised.
decided.refundBody: It has been decided to refund 100% of what was raised for “{initiative}”. Each contribution goes back to its original payment method, in batches; you can follow progress in the dashboard.
decided.votePreheader: The people who donated decide what happens to what was raised.
decided.voteTitle: Decided: we are asking the people who donated
decided.voteBody: The vote on “{initiative}” has been launched. Donors can vote until {date}; anyone who asks for a refund has it under way as soon as they vote, and anyone who does not vote will be refunded when it closes.

closed.wonPreheader: The vote has chosen a project. Time to pay out.
closed.wonTitle: The vote has chosen a project
closed.wonBody: In “{initiative}”, “{option}” won. The new goal is {amount}: what those who voted for a project option contributed (those who did not vote or asked for a refund have been refunded).
closed.wonNext: KORUM’s fee goes down in the same proportion. To pay out you need, as always, the invoice and both signatures.
closed.refundSubject: The vote on “{initiative}” ends without a project
closed.reasonNO_VOTES: The vote on “{initiative}” has ended with no votes for any project option.
closed.reasonTIE: The vote on “{initiative}” has ended in a tie.
closed.reasonNOTHING_LEFT: After the refunds requested, nothing is left in “{initiative}” to carry out the project.
closed.refundNext: As planned, everyone who contributed gets 100% back, to their original payment method.

poll.subject: You decide: what should we do with “{initiative}”?
poll.preheader: Vote until {date}. You can also ask for your contribution back.
poll.title: Your vote decides
poll.body: “{initiative}” from {organization} did not reach its goal. Before refunding the money, {organization} wants to know whether you would rather carry out a smaller version of the project with what was raised.
poll.rules: One vote per person, until {date}. The most voted option wins and is carried out with what those who vote for a project contributed. If you do not vote, we refund 100%. This link is only yours: please don’t forward it.
poll.refund: If you would rather get your contribution back, choose “I’d rather have my contribution back”: we refund it in full, whatever happens.

result.subject: “{initiative}” is going ahead
result.preheader: Thanks to the families at {organization} who voted.
result.title: It’s going ahead!
result.body: The vote on “{initiative}” has chosen: “{option}”. It will be carried out with what those of you who voted contributed, including your contribution.
result.next: The money stays in the initiative’s money box at PAYCOMET until two people from {organization} sign the payout. When it is done, we will show you the Before and After.

refunding.subject: We are refunding your contribution to “{initiative}”
refunding.preheader: It goes back in full to your original payment method.
refunding.title: We are refunding 100%
refunding.body: “{initiative}” from {organization} did not reach its goal, so we are refunding everything you contributed, including the voluntary contribution to KORUM if you made one.
refunding.how: It goes back to your original payment method (card or Bizum) without you having to do anything. We will let you know when it is done; it may take a few days to show on your card or in Bizum.

cookies.title: Optional cookies
cookies.text: We use cookies that are not essential. They only switch on if you accept them; if you decline, KORUM works exactly the same.

finder.label: Name of your school, club or organisation
finder.hint: Type at least 2 letters. Search by name, town, postcode or province.
finder.results: {count, plural, one {# organisation found} other {# organisations found}}
finder.error: We could not run the search right now.
finder.emptyText: Your organisation may not be on KORUM yet. Registering it is free and takes a few minutes.
finder.noResults: No results. You can register your organisation for free.

calculator.objectiveLabel: What do you want to achieve?
calculator.costHint: This is an example amount: replace it with your own quote.

colegios.title: Fundraising for schools and parents’ groups
colegios.description: Fund climate control, shade or digital whiteboards with all-or-nothing campaigns, double signatures and a 100% refund if the goal is not reached.
colegios.h1: How to fund improvements at your school without handling cash
colegios.answer: KORUM lets a school or its parents’ association propose an improvement, approve it with a double signature and fund it with families’ contributions in an all-or-nothing campaign: if the goal is not reached, 100% is refunded to each person. The first {exempt} of each school year pays no commission.

sections.title: What your school can do
bullets: Open an ideas box with a quorum so families can propose and back improvements.
Launch all-or-nothing campaigns for climate control, playground shade, digital whiteboards or the end-of-year trip.
Sell tickets and raffle tickets with QR codes at festivals and parties, with capacity control.
Set class challenges (from the first year of nursery to the last year of compulsory secondary school) and celebrate what is achieved.
Export Model 182 in one click if the organisation falls under Law 49/2002.

sections.title: Who signs and who gets paid
paragraphs: A state school always takes part through its parents’ association, which is the organisation that owns the funds. Subsidised and private schools register through their owner.

Approving an idea and releasing funds requires the signatures of two different people: the head of the school and the chair of the parents’ association. Money is collected through Paycomet, held until the goal is reached, and paid to the organisation or directly to its supplier with the invoice in hand.

sections.title: Complete freedom to choose your supplier
paragraphs: KORUM never intermediates or approves suppliers of works or equipment, and never charges them commissions. Your organisation enters the quote from the supplier it prefers and the platform works out the goal.

sections.title: Class challenges, always positive
paragraphs: Classes add participating families to unlock a shared prize. What is achieved is celebrated (“Class 3B already has 28 families”); nobody is singled out and amounts are never compared between classes.

comoFunciona.title: How the platform works
comoFunciona.description: From idea to improvement in 4 steps: ideas with a quorum, double signature, all-or-nothing contributions via Paycomet and a 100% refund if not reached.
comoFunciona.h1: How KORUM works, step by step
comoFunciona.answer: On KORUM a community proposes an improvement, backs it with signatures, two people from the organisation approve it and families fund it with all-or-nothing contributions: the money is collected through Paycomet and, if the goal is not reached in time, 100% is refunded to each person.

steps.title: Propose and gather signatures
steps.text: A family proposes an idea under a private alias. Others back it with their signature until the quorum is reached.

steps.title: Double signature by the organisation
steps.text: Two different people from the organisation approve the idea. The organisation freely chooses its supplier and the platform works out the goal.

steps.title: Families contribute in 10 seconds
steps.text: With Bizum or card and just their email. Every initiative has its own identified pot and a deadline.

steps.title: Enjoy the Before and After
steps.text: When the goal is reached, the improvement is paid for with the supplier’s invoice in hand and the result is published.

sections.title: What happens to the money
paragraphs: Payments are processed by Paycomet and the money is held until the goal is reached. KORUM records it in a double-entry ledger, to the cent. If the last contribution takes the total above the goal, the surplus goes in full to the organisation as an additional project reserve.

sections.title: And if the goal is not reached
paragraphs: A campaign lasts at most {maxDays} days. If it does not reach 100% in that time and the organisation does not decide to resize it, Paycomet automatically refunds 100% of what was collected to each person, voluntary contribution included, to the original payment method.

seguridad.title: Security and transparency
seguridad.description: Who handles the money, how spending is approved, what happens if the goal is not reached and how your data is protected on KORUM.
seguridad.h1: Security and transparency: who handles the money and the data
seguridad.answer: Payments are processed by PAYCOMET, a payment institution authorised by the Bank of Spain. KORUM is the technology: it never holds your money. Every initiative has its own identified pot, and the money is held at Paycomet until the goal is reached.

sections.title: What KORUM is and is not
paragraphs: KORUM is a technology platform: it is not a financial institution and does not hold funds. Payments, the holding of funds, transfers and refunds are carried out by Paycomet.
KORUM never intermediates or approves suppliers of works or equipment and never charges them commissions: each organisation chooses freely.

sections.title: How spending is approved
paragraphs: Approving an idea and releasing funds requires the signatures of two different people from the organisation, both with two-step verification. Payment is made with the supplier’s invoice in hand and recorded in a ledger that cannot be edited: mistakes are corrected with a reversing entry.

sections.title: If the goal is not reached
paragraphs: 100% of what was collected is refunded to each person, to the original payment method and automatically.

sections.title: Your data
bullets: No tracking cookies or third-party pixels: visit analytics do not use cookies.
The tax ID provided for the tax certificate is stored encrypted.
Families’ ideas and the payment process are not indexed by search engines.
Before and After photos are only published if the organisation confirms that no recognisable minors appear.
You can ask for a copy or the deletion of your data at any time.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.description: Clear answers on money, refunds, double signatures, commissions, raffles, tax certificates and personal data on KORUM.
faq.answer: Here we answer, in plain language, what organisations, families and businesses ask us most.

faq.a: Paycomet, a payment institution authorised by the Bank of Spain, processes payments and holds the money until the goal is reached. KORUM is the technology and does not hold your money.

faq.q: What happens if the goal is not reached?
faq.a: 100% of what was collected is refunded to each person, to the original payment method and automatically, including the voluntary contribution to KORUM.

faq.q: What happens if the goal is exceeded?
faq.a: The initiative is marked as achieved, closes to new contributions and the surplus goes in full to the organisation as an additional project reserve.

faq.q: How long does a campaign last?
faq.a: At most {maxDays} days from publication, because Paycomet only allows funds to be split within a limited period after each payment.
Registration is free. The first {exempt} of each school year pays no commission; after that, from {t1Rate} to {t3Rate} depending on the size of the initiative. Full rates are on the pricing page.
Yes, always through its parents’ association, which is the organisation that owns the funds. Subsidised and private schools do so through their owner.

faq.q: Can we choose our own supplier?
faq.a: Yes, always. KORUM never intermediates or approves suppliers of works or equipment and never charges them commissions.
Two different people: the main manager (head teacher, club chair…) and a co-signer (chair of the parents’ association, club treasurer…). Both are needed to approve an idea and to release funds.

Yes, with numbered tickets and a certified on-screen draw. Raffles are regulated by each autonomous community and may require prior notification or authorisation: the organisation confirms it complies with its own rules before publishing.

faq.q: Do I need to sign up to contribute?
faq.a: No. To contribute or buy tickets, your email is enough, and that is where your receipt or tickets arrive instantly. To propose or sign ideas you do need a verified account.

faq.q: Will I receive a tax certificate?
faq.a: Only if the organisation has its Law 49/2002 status accredited. Otherwise you receive a named contribution receipt.

faq.q: What does a sponsoring business receive?
faq.a: It appears as a friendly business in its category (Gold, Silver or Bronze), receives the sponsorship receipt and the fee invoice straight away, and 100% of the chosen level reaches the initiative.
We do not use tracking cookies, the tax ID is stored encrypted, and you can ask for a copy or the deletion of your data whenever you like.

help.title: Frequently asked questions and support
help.intro: Here are the most common questions. If yours is not here, write to us: the school or the KORUM team will answer, depending on the topic.

guarantee.q: What does the voluntary contribution to KORUM include?
guarantee.a: It is optional and changes nothing about your donation. It keeps the service running that guarantees every family that 100% of the donation reaches the school without bank deductions, the automatic refund if the goal is not reached, and the automatic issue of your certificate or receipt.

family.q: Can both parents sign from the same device?
family.a: Yes. Up to two family accounts can sign from the same phone or computer and count as verified signatures. If suspicious patterns are detected (for example, many different accounts from one device), those signatures are flagged and do not add to the count until they are reviewed.

refund.q: What happens if the initiative does not reach its goal?
refund.a: You get 100% of what you paid back, including the voluntary contribution, on your card or original payment method. You do not need to ask: the refund is automatic.

payments.a: Payments, holds and refunds are carried out by PAYCOMET, a payment institution authorised by the Bank of Spain. KORUM is a technology platform: it is not a financial institution and does not hold funds. The money stays held at PAYCOMET until the goal is reached.

fiscal.q: Do I get a tax certificate for my donation?
fiscal.a: It depends on the organisation. If it falls under Law 49/2002 and has proven it, you receive a donation certificate (we need your tax ID, which is optional). If not, you receive a named contribution receipt with no tax effect. Tickets and raffles never give a certificate.

ideas.q: Is my proposal in the ideas box anonymous?
ideas.a: Yes. The school and other families only see a code like #FAM-1234, never your name or email. You can talk to the school from “My account”, under “My proposals and signatures”; please do not write names in the messages.

hucha.q: What is My Piggy Bank, and is money kept in it?
hucha.a: My Piggy Bank is a scheduled monthly contribution: you choose an amount and an organisation, and each month your card is charged and the money goes to an open initiative. No balance is kept. You can pause or cancel it in one click from “My Piggy Bank”.

data.q: How do I exercise my rights over my data?
data.a: From “My account” you can download your data, withdraw consents and delete your account. To correct your name or email, use the form on this page with the topic “Correct my personal data”: we will answer within a month.

independence.q: Does KORUM choose the contractors for the works?
independence.a: No. Each organisation freely chooses its own supplier, and KORUM does not intermediate or charge commissions to contractors or equipment suppliers.
